title: Chronological chatstream traffic emulator for cross-tenant p95 & tokens/sec regression detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a streaming chat/completions traffic emulator that replays realistic, time-ordered user sessions across SSE and WebSocket protocols. The emulator must be KV-cache aware (support priming and prefix reuse), maintain chronological session relationships (stitching messages by real timestamps), and produce metrics useful for tokens/sec, p95 latency, and regression detection pipelines.
background: Existing stream load drivers generate independent short-lived sessions and synthetic tokenflows that miss two important production characteristics: chronological interleaving of user sessions (which affects KV cache hit distribution) and tenant-level fanout similarity. Several recent regressions were only visible after long tail workload reconstruction. This ticket aims to close that gap with a replay-style emulator that can drive hundreds of thousands of concurrent streams with realistic timestamp distributions and KV priming windows.
goals: 1) Emulate time-ordered chat sessions (stitching) with realistic pause/resume behavior; 2) Surface p95 regressions under KV-cache-sensitive workloads; 3) Produce stable tokens/sec measurements with confidence intervals; 4) Integrate with regression detector to automatically flag SLO deviations; 5) Support both SSE and WebSocket clients and multiplexing modes.
acceptance_criteria: - Simulator can run 200k concurrent logical sessions across SSE and WS on dedicated test cluster; - Generated workload reproduces historical KV hit-rate patterns within ±5% of production sample for a 24h window; - p95 latency and tokens/sec metrics emitted to metrics pipeline (Prometheus/ClickHouse) every 5m; - Regression detector (alerting threshold: 12% increase in p95 or 15% drop in tokens/sec sustained over 15m) triggers a CI alert and creates an issue; - Documentation + runbook committed and reviewed.
technical_design:
High-level components:
- Session Replayer: reads a compressed session trace (chronological events), replays messages preserving original inter-event times with configurable time-scaling (real-time, 2x, burst-scaling).
- KV Priming Engine: injects artificial prefix calls to warm KV caches for selected sessions and marks cache-lifecycle events so runtime can correlate cache hits to observed latency.
- Protocol Layer: pluggable client implementations for SSE and WebSocket with support for multiplexed connections and backpressure simulation.
- Orchestrator: assigns sessions to worker pools respecting tenancy and per-tenant fanout distributions.
- Metrics Exporter: emits tokens/sec, p95, p50, error-rates, connect/disconnect churn, and KV-hit-ratio.
Design trade-offs: lightweight Go binary (low memory) vs richer Python scenario definitions. We chose Go for scale and low GC jitter. To keep UI-friendly scenario authoring we will accept scenario DSL (YAML) instead of full Python SDK.
Resource concerns: each worker process pins a libuv loop and maintains up to 10k multiplexed WS connections; plan capacity accordingly.
test_plan: - Unit tests for session stitcher and KV priming logic; - Integration harness in dev cluster with 10k sessions validating metrics pipeline ingestion; - Scale test in prod-like staging (target 200k logical sessions) with progressive ramp (5k -> 25k -> 100k -> 200k) and inter-run anomaly detection; - Regression gate: run replay suite against last known-good runtime image; if p95 increases >12% or tokens/sec drops >15% for two consecutive 5m windows, mark as regression; - Chaos experiments: inject node GC pauses and connection churn to verify graceful degradation and fallback metrics.
runbook_steps:
1) Prepare scenario: point to session-trace S3 path and config YAML (kv_priming: true, time_scale: 4x, tenant_mix: default).
2) Start orchestrator: ./emulator --scenario ... --target-concurrency 100000 --protocol ws
3) Monitor metrics: tokens/sec (emulator.metrics.tokens), p95 (emulator.metrics.p95.latency_ms), kv_hit_ratio.
4) If regression detector fires: capture heap/pprof dump from worker nodes, collect a 60s packet capture from edge, tag run_id and open ENG-Triage issue with links.
5) Post-run: run analysis script to compute sample standard error for tokens/sec and p95; upload artifacts to Drive.
progress_updates:
2025-11-20: initial spike prototype (single process) validated chronological replay and KV priming markers; observed expected increase in KV-hit-ratio for primed sessions.
2025-12-05: replaced Python driver with Go prototype to remove GC jitter; confirmed stable token emission in 10k-session run.
2026-01-14: integrated Prometheus exporter and ClickHouse ingestion; dashboards created (dash id: emu-chron-001).
2026-02-02: early scale test reached 75k logical sessions; uncovered connection pooling bug in orchestrator where multiplexed connections leaked. Rafal fixed orchestrator pooling (PR #4342).
2026-02-27: ran 150k-session run with synthetic churn; p95 baseline increased by 9% vs historical 24h replay; no regression alert (below 12%).
2026-03-08: added regression-detector wiring to CI and PagerDuty endpoint; first intentional regression test (kernel patch) triggered alert as expected.
2026-03-10: currently tuning surge annealing and reducing CPU syscall overhead; planning final 200k verification run.
review_feedback:
- PM requested clearer tenant isolation knobs (added tenant_mix parameter).
- SRE asked for per-process self-healing on repeated TCP failures (implemented exponential backoff and circuit breaker).
- Design reviewed by Runtime team: approved using Go and YAML DSL, asked to add signature verification on scenario artifacts (accepted).
open_issues_and_risks:
- Risk: head-of-line blocking for long-lived WS connections under extreme multiplexing; mitigation: limit per-connection multiplex factor and spread tenants across connections.
- Risk: synthetic traces may not cover extreme long-tail user think-times; mitigation: include heavy-tailed pause distributions (Pareto) in scenario generator.
- Operational: need a low-cost teardown path to avoid runaway billing during 200k runs.
next_steps: 1) Finalize surge annealing params and run full 200k verification on 2026-03-18; 2) Create Confluence doc with scenario DSL and example traces; 3) Add nightly 3h replay runs with automated regression checks; 4) Hand off runbook to SRE and Performance guild.
results_snapshot:
Latest 150k run (2026-02-27) metrics:
- sustained tokens/sec (cluster): 1.8M ± 4.1% (95% CI)
- request p95 latency: 285ms (baseline historical: 260ms)
- kv_hit_ratio (primed cohort): 72% vs unprimed 18%
- error_rate: 0.07% (mostly transient 5xx on one node)
Regression detector: no automatic regression triggered (threshold 12% p95 increase).
